# Set compensation bands and review pay

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When hiring levels, roles or locations require a consistent compensation framework. An approved role-and-location pay framework with documented exceptions and an owned review cycle.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Inventory roles and current compensation

agent-runnable


Collect role scope, level, work location, employment arrangement and current cash and equity terms in a restricted workspace. Normalize hours and currencies and separate guaranteed pay from variable or contingent awards.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Build a documented comparison and cost model

agent-runnable


Compare relevant market evidence and internal role scope, and model payroll cost and affordability. Record source dates, sample limits and exchange assumptions instead of treating a vendor estimate as a required rate.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Review fairness and applicable local constraints

human · human approval required


HR, finance and advisers assess pay equity, local minimums, disclosure duties and contractual constraints. Investigate unexplained differences and distinguish a performance assessment from a protected personal characteristic.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve bands and individual exceptions

human · human approval required


Leadership approves the framework, budget, exception authority and review cadence. Obtain appropriate approvals before offering, changing or promising compensation or equity to a person.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Record changes and monitor the framework

agent-runnable


Reconcile approved changes with contracts, payroll and grant processes. Communicate only the authorized individual terms and track exceptions, hiring feedback and the next review.

- Verify: An approved role-and-location pay framework with documented exceptions and an owned review cycle.
- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance)
